items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: Oh, I worked with Buddy Rich during that time, too... in fact, Buddy and I did call me up to do a commercial for Alcoa Aluminum, just bass and drums

ctx.x: What kind of instrument was it?

It was an old German flatback bass; the same bass that he used. Anyway, I started gigging at Riverside and people started calling me; my Buddy De Franco called me for a week, and I got my union card straight, my New York card straight, for that engagement down at the Cafe Bohemia -- that was a popular spot, in the Village.

Oh, from there, I started -- I was working so much, making money but I wasn't realizing any of it because I was going after that stuff, but I was recording almost every day; I had matinees to play; I mean, one week working with Buddy, the next week they wanted me to work down in Birdland, on a Sunday, and I'm rehearsing late that afternoon with Gigi Gryce, Donald Byrd and, oh, I forgot the piano player's name, but they formed a group; they made an album that I was supposed to make ... I was so tired I couldn't…
